metadata.scenario_context: Jennifer is excited to settle into her new flat and has decided to throw a warming party. She recently found out that her new next door is used to attracting very loud parties. Her colleagues, Simon and Matthew, are set to attend Jennifer's party.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Armenia would like to have heavy drinkers as neighbors.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Armenia would not like to have heavy drinkers as neighbors.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss bringing marigolds to Jennifer’s housewarming party.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether would like to have heavy drinkers as a neighbor.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide appropriate gift to bring to Jennifer’s housewarming party.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss on whether it’s acceptable to have heavy drinkers  as a neighbor.

shared_prefix.speaker: Simon
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Matthew, are you excited about Jennifer's housewarming party? I was thinking of bringing some marigolds. They could really brighten up her new place. What do you think? 

Also, what’s your take on having heavy drinkers as neighbors? I feel like it could add to the vibe, don’t you?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Matthew
shared_prefix.message:
Marigolds sound nice... they would definitely brighten the place. I was thinking of bringing something more traditional, like sweets. But marigolds are a good choice. 

As for heavy drinkers... I really don’t like the idea. It can lead to noise and disturbances. I mean, it’s not really a comfortable atmosphere, is it?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Simon
shared_prefix.message:
I appreciate that you like the marigolds idea. They really do have that *uplifting* effect. 

About heavy drinkers, I see your point, but I think it can create a fun atmosphere. I mean, a little noise is just part of having a good time, right? Wouldn't you want that excitement next door?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Matthew
shared_prefix.message: Actually, that’s not how it works in our culture. We value a peaceful, respectful environment. Noise and chaos aren’t considered fun; they’re disruptive. Heavy drinkers next door? It’s just not acceptable. It’s not about excitement; it's about having a proper atmosphere. Fun doesn’t mean losing control or disturbing others.
shared_prefix.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Simon
turns.message:
I get where you're coming from, but I still think having heavy drinkers can bring a lively energy. It’s all about perspective, really. I mean, what's wrong with a little *celebration*? 

And let’s not forget about the marigolds! They’ll definitely complement that vibe, don't you think?
turns.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Matthew
turns.message:
I understand your perspective, but I still believe that excessive drinking isn't the right kind of celebration. It can lead to problems for everyone involved. A good atmosphere doesn’t have to be loud or chaotic. 

As for the marigolds, yes, they’ll look nice regardless of the vibe. But I just wish for a neighbor who can enjoy gatherings without causing disturbances. That’s what matters more to me.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Simon
turns.message:
I respect your thoughts on celebration, but I still think a lively neighbor adds *character* to a community. I mean, isn't that part of the fun of living next to others? 

And yes, the marigolds will be a great touch, either way. I just think there's something to be said for embracing a bit of noise. Wouldn't you agree?
turns.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Matthew
turns.message:
Character doesn’t have to come from noise or chaos. A good neighbor can have fun without being loud or disruptive. It's about respect for each other’s space. I just prefer a calmer environment. 

And yes, the marigolds will be a nice touch, but I really hope for neighbors who value peace. That’s what creates a good community for me.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Simon
turns.message:
I see your point about respect, but I still believe that a bit of liveliness can enhance the community experience. I mean, it’s all about balance, right? 

The marigolds will definitely help set a pleasant scene, but I think having a neighbor who enjoys celebrations adds a unique flavor to the mix. Don't you think a little excitement can coexist with peace?
turns.label: Minimization

turns.speaker: Matthew
turns.message:
Balance is important, but that doesn’t mean accepting disruptive behavior. There’s a difference between liveliness and chaos. I don’t think excitement should come at the expense of peace. 

I appreciate the marigolds will create a pleasant scene, but I really just want neighbors who understand the value of a quiet, respectful environment. That's the kind of mix I prefer.
turns.label: Acceptance
